clue.text: Impound a Scotsman's cow and young dog ?

parts.note: in Scots speech a cow is a 'coo'
a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a Scottish farmer's cow and puppy, as if bailiffs had come to call.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to shut animals in an enclosure, the same as penning them in a hutch.

clue.text: A singularly stable sort of town ?

definitions.text: A singularly stable sort of town

parts.words: A singularly stable sort of town
parts.note: a stable holding just a single horse, and the dismissive phrase for a small dull town

explanation.surface: A remark about a town that never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like 'steady', but means a building for horses; 'singularly' says there is only one in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is a tiny, backward place with little going on.

clue.text: That 'holier than thou attitude is just about right porcine

indicators.note: 'about' means the pig word wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: porcine means pig-like, piggish

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious attitude is said to be rather like a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link; 'about' puts PIGGISH round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctimonious person behaves as if morally superior, the self-righteous stance of a prig.

clue.text: It gives the writer a hot dinner

definitions.text: It gives the writer a hot dinner

parts.words: It gives the writer a hot dinner
parts.note: a book churned out only to keep the author's cooking pot on the boil, that is to pay for food

explanation.surface: Something seems to provide an author with a cooked meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A potboiler is hack writing done for money, to 'keep the pot boiling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hastily written book produced only for income keeps food on the author's table.

clue.text: Elf's hide-out when Oberon and Titania quarrel

definitions.text: Elf's hide-out when Oberon and Titania quarrel

parts.words: Elf's hide-out when Oberon and Titania quarrel
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck says that when the fairy king and queen quarrel, their elves creep in fear into the cups of oak nuts and hide there

explanation.surface: A question about where a fairy shelters during a royal row in Shakespeare's wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Shakespeare: 'all their elves for fear / Creep into acorn cups and hide them there' (A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 2).
explanation.definitionFit: The scaly cup holding an oak nut is small enough to shelter a tiny fairy in the play.

clue.text: Minute splashdown

parts.note: a tiny bit of liquid falling into the sea, a phrase for an insignificant amount

explanation.surface: A spacecraft returns to Earth in a tiny landing at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' is the adjective tiny, not sixty seconds, and 'splashdown' suggests a space capsule landing at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an amount too small to make any difference, like one bead of water lost in the sea.

clue.text: Singularly game, he who successfully dared Cape Horn

definitions.text: he who successfully dared Cape Horn

explanation.surface: A brave sailor who sailed round the southern tip of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a bat-and-ball game, so 'singularly' drops its final letter; one who sails round a cape has rounded it.

clue.text: 150 got with a last wild volley-that's pretty steep

indicators.note: the remaining letters come last, after the numerals

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches 150 with a final reckless swing, and a commentator calls it a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns VOLLEY into OVELLY, placed last after CL. Clovelly is a pretty Devon fishing village whose cobbled street drops steeply to the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon village is famous for being picturesque and for its very steep main street.

clue.text: Promote non-polluting transport

parts.note: to promote is to push, and clean transport is the pedal bicycle

explanation.surface: A green campaign slogan urging people to support clean travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a campaign slogan: 'push' means promote and 'bike' is the clean transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal bicycle, as opposed to a motorbike, burns no fuel and gives off no fumes.

clue.text: Range record

explanation.surface: A pairing that could be a heading in a cooker manual or an archive.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice's register is its compass of notes; a register is also an official written list.

clue.text: Red's plea to Slater, say

indicators.note: 'say' signals that the words are spoken, and the pronounced phrase gives the entry

parts.note: a slater lays slates on roofs, so a householder's request to one is 'roof us'

explanation.surface: A left-winger appeals to someone named Slater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a communist and 'Slater' like a surname, but the slater is a roofer. The 's means 'is', so the definition reads 'Red is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufous is a naturalist's word for a reddish-brown colour, as in the rufous hummingbird.

clue.text: " The Weasels "?

parts.note: the quotation marks make the words look like the name of a band, and the nursery song says 'pop goes the weasel'

explanation.surface: A title in quotation marks, as if naming a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The song line 'Pop goes the weasel' makes Weasels a likely name for a band of the pop kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of chart musicians performs under a name like this one.

clue.text: Braved in a way to express a way

indicators.note: 'in a way' says the letters of the first word are arranged in another fashion

explanation.surface: Someone faced danger in a particular manner of expressing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BRAVED is signalled by 'in a way', and the definition plays on the same words: such a part of speech tells how something is done.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of speech, such as 'quickly', modifies a verb to say how an action is done.

clue.text: That old gag, concerning a car

definitions.text: That old gag, concerning a car

parts.words: That old gag, concerning a car
parts.note: a gag puts someone's voice out of action, and the exhaust part fitted to a motor muffles its noise

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a tired joke about motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old gag' looks like a stale joke, but a gag also stops speech; the exhaust device on a car does the same for engine noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler that quietens an engine or a gun is the device that stops noise, as a gag stops a voice.

clue.text: Would suit 'anybody's book that Fleet Street should close down

definitions.text: Would suit 'anybody's book that Fleet Street should close down

parts.words: Would suit 'anybody's book that Fleet Street should close down
parts.note: a betting phrase 'suits my book' meets the leaves pasted inside a book's covers, read as the newspapers ending

explanation.surface: A remark that anyone would welcome the closure of the London newspaper district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit anybody's book' is an idiom for 'please anyone', but every book needs these sheets inside its covers; Fleet Street was the home of London's newspapers, so closing it would end the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank leaves glued inside a hardback's front and back covers are part of every bound book.

clue.text: Acronymically Laban's elder and homelier daughter

definitions.text: Acronymically Laban's elder and homelier daughter

indicators.note: acronymically means the following words are reduced to their initial letters, as an acronym is built

explanation.surface: A biblical aside about the plainer of Laban's two girls.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Laban's elder daughter was 'tender eyed' while her sister Rachel was beautiful, and Jacob was tricked into marrying her first; the initials of the clue's words spell her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names Laban's firstborn girl, Jacob's first wife and Rachel's sister, with these four letters.

clue.text: Old knight at sale, of, his effects?

definitions.text: Old knight at sale, of, his effects?

parts.words: Old knight at sale, of, his effects?
parts.note: an auction lot made of a knight's weapon, his spear, makes the name of an Arthurian knight

explanation.surface: An auction of a dead knight's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: A lance is a knight's weapon, and an item at an auction is a lot; together they name Arthur's most famous knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot du Lac was the foremost knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Mail-order pioneer ?.

parts.note: chain mail is body armour, so someone who first made orders of mail was a maker of armour

explanation.surface: A tribute to the inventor of catalogue shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail-order' suggests catalogue shopping, but mail here is chain mail, the metal mesh worn by knights.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith who makes armour, mail included, filled orders for mail long before catalogue shopping.

clue.text: Justice will be coming round for Jane

definitions.text: Justice will be coming round for Jane

parts.words: Justice will be coming round for Jane
parts.note: medieval judges travelled a circuit called by this old word, and it is also the surname of Charlotte Bronte's heroine Jane

explanation.surface: A judge is about to visit a woman named Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Justices 'in eyre' were medieval judges who rode a circuit round the counties, so justice came round on it; Jane's surname comes from Charlotte Bronte's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The old legal word means a judge's circuit, and Bronte gave it as surname to her governess heroine.

clue.text: This man's sold out

parts.note: a trader who sends goods out of the country sells them abroad

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper has run out of stock, or a principled man has betrayed his ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sold out' suggests nothing left or a betrayal, but read it as 'sold outside the country'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who ships goods for sale abroad sells them out of the country.

clue.text: Said " Be sure 'to come and baby-sit again. She did

definitions.text: Said " Be sure 'to come and baby-sit again. She did

parts.words: Said " Be sure 'to come and baby-sit again. She did
parts.note: a parent prompted someone not to forget, and the sitter looked after the children a second time

explanation.surface: A parent asks the babysitter to come back, and she does.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two readings: prompting someone to remember, and 're-minded', that is minded the children again.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's memory about a duty is to prompt them; to mind children again is to babysit once more.

clue.text: Be on the beaten track, or doth wrong to farm stock

indicators.note: the two words are set wrong, that is put into a different order

parts.note: an ox is a beast of farm livestock

explanation.surface: A farmer's advice to stick to tradition, or else harm the cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges OR DOTH to ORTHOD, then OX is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional or accepted views follow the well-trodden path rather than straying from it.

clue.text: The islands in South Pacific

parts.note: the collective name for the island groups of the central and south Pacific, including Polynesia and Melanesia

explanation.surface: A reference to the setting of the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: South Pacific was a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical set on an island, but the clue means the region's island groups as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The region takes in Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia and often Australasia, the islands of the Pacific.

clue.text: Don't be overdoing things at this

definitions.text: Don't be overdoing things at this

parts.words: Don't be overdoing things at this
parts.note: overdoing the food at a kitchen stove means cooking it too long

explanation.surface: A warning against overworking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overdoing things' sounds like advice about stress, but here it means overcooking food on a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: The stove with an oven and hob is where food is overdone or burnt.

clue.text: As Elijah was conducted before the people

definitions.text: As Elijah was conducted before the people

parts.words: As Elijah was conducted before the people
parts.note: Mendelssohn's Elijah is a sacred choral work, performed under a conductor before an audience

explanation.surface: The prophet Elijah is led out in front of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophet Elijah seems to be escorted before a crowd, but the clue means Mendelssohn's choral work 'Elijah' being performed to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's Elijah is a large sacred work for chorus, soloists and orchestra, sung without staging.

clue.text: Tempting to see the end of a Honolulu toll

indicators.note: the end of the city's name is its closing pair of letters, which repeat its earlier syllable

parts.note: a bell tolls, or rings

explanation.surface: A traveller is keen to get past the last charge on a Hawaiian road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes the last two letters of Honolulu, LU.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring and tempting both mean enticing someone with a bait or promise.

clue.text: On this happening I'd look away from the afterglow

definitions.text: On this happening I'd look away from the afterglow

parts.words: On this happening I'd look away from the afterglow
parts.note: the clue holds a happening and the word I'd, and the afterglow is seen at the close of day

explanation.surface: Someone says they would avert their eyes from a sunset glow when something occurs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue holds pieces of the answer, EVENT (happening) and I'D, and the afterglow follows sunset, at the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, when the sky glows after sunset.

clue.text: Artemisia finds Jack poorly clad

parts.note: a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor
someone poorly clad has only a rag on

explanation.surface: A woman named Artemisia discovers that Jack is shabbily dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Artemisia looks like a woman's name, but it is the genus of wormwood herbs; the culinary herb in it is Artemisia dracunculus.
explanation.definitionFit: The aniseed-flavoured kitchen herb belongs to the wormwood genus, Artemisia.

clue.text: Walked, while the best of men got a lift

parts.note: a saint is the best of men, abbreviated ST
to get a lift in a vehicle or on a horse is to ride, past tense rode

explanation.surface: Someone went on foot while the groom's best men were driven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the best of men' looks like a best man at a wedding, but it is a saint, ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode is the past of stride, to walk with long steps.
